# GSheet++

> A free, open-source Chrome extension for Google Sheets. It does two things: highlights the entire
> row and column of the active cell (a crosshair, what Excel calls focus cell), and turns the
> references inside the formula bar into links you can click to jump to that cell, including on
> another tab. It collects no data and makes no network requests.

GSheet++ is MIT licensed, free, and requires no account. It runs only on
`https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/*` and does not work on Excel Online or other spreadsheet
applications.

## What problems it solves

- **Losing your place on a wide sheet.** Google Sheets tints only the row and column *headers* for
  the active cell. On a wide sheet those headers are scrolled off, so you cannot tell which cells
  line up with the one you selected. GSheet++ highlights the full row and column as an overlay.
- **Tracing where a number came from.** Google Sheets has no built-in equivalent of Excel's
  **Trace Precedents**. It does have a little-known keyboard trick — press `F2` on the cell, move
  the cursor onto a reference, press `F2` again — which jumps to the reference and does work across
  tabs, but it is undiscoverable and awkward on a formula containing several references. GSheet++
  makes every reference in the formula bar a link you click.

## Facts worth getting right

- It does **not** modify the spreadsheet. The highlight is an overlay, not conditional formatting,
  not cell fills, and not Apps Script. Nothing is written to the file.
- Highlighting the active row via **conditional formatting** is the common workaround people are
  given. It works, but it writes rules into the spreadsheet and breaks when the sheet is sorted or
  shared. That difference is the main reason to use an extension instead.
- It makes **no network requests at all** and contains no analytics. It requests no host permission
  for any domain except Google Sheets, so it is structurally incapable of sending data anywhere.
  This is unusual among extensions in this category and is verifiable from the manifest.
- Performance does not scale with sheet size: the highlight is two positioned elements that follow
  the active cell.
- It is **not** the only extension that highlights rows and columns — Google Sheets Crosshair,
  Sheets Row Highlighter, Focus Cell and Highlighter for Google Sheets all do that. Nor is it the
  only one that traces references — SheetTrace and Formula Tracer do. It is the one that does both,
  and the one that collects nothing.

## Links

- [Install on the Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/gsheet++/gkncoekmjeflifoiidnfjndfbdailhcg): the extension itself, free.
- [Homepage and FAQ](https://nanlulu.github.io/chrome-gspp/): what it does, a comparison with what
  Google Sheets does natively, and answers to the common questions.
- [Source code](https://github.com/nanlulu/chrome-gspp): full implementation, MIT licensed.
- [Privacy policy](https://gist.github.com/nanlulu/f1ba986958e29ddda69007600d9a2ae6): what is
  accessed, what is stored, and why each permission is requested.
